Each factor 1 - x^{1/k} ~ -(1/k)(x-1) = (1/k)(1-x) as x->1? Since x^{1/k}=1 + (x-1)/k + o, so 1 - x^{1/k} = -(x-1)/k + o = (1-x)/k + o. Product over k=2..n gives (1-x)^{n-1} * product_{k=2}^n 1/k = (1-x)^{n-1}/n!. Denominator (1-x)^{n-1}. Limit = 1/n! . Need check sign: (1-x)^{n-1} for even/odd? As x->1 both sides same. answer_text:
We have

\[
\lim_{x\to 1}\frac{(1-x^{1/2})(1-x^{1/3})\cdots(1-x^{1/n})}{(1-x)^{n-1}}.
\]

There are \(n-1\) factors in the numerator, so we can rewrite the expression as a product:

\[
\prod_{k=2}^n \frac{1-x^{1/k}}{1-x}.
\]

Now evaluate each limit as \(x\to 1\). Since

\[
x^{1/k}=1+\frac{x-1}{k}+o(x-1),
\]

we get

\[
1-x^{1/k}
=1-\left(1+\frac{x-1}{k}+o(x-1)\right)
= -\frac{x-1}{k}+o(x-1).
\]

But \(-\frac{x-1}{k}=\frac{1-x}{k}\), so

\[
\frac{1-x^{1/k}}{1-x}\to \frac1k
\qquad\text{as }x\to 1.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\lim_{x\to 1}\prod_{k=2}^n \frac{1-x^{1/k}}{1-x}
=
\prod_{k=2}^n \frac1k
=
\frac{1}{2\cdot 3\cdots n}
=
\frac{1}{n!}.
\]

Thus,

\[
\boxed{\frac{1}{n!}}
\]

27B·v4.method: Asymptotic expansion of each factor (1−x^{1/k}) ~ (1−x)/k, then product of coefficients yields 1/n!.
